cases.prompt: Draft a JF abstract from these notes. Do not ask a follow-up; use visible placeholders where the evidence is missing.
provided_facts: Question: whether supplier concentration is associated with corporate cash holdings.
Data: Compustat firms, but the years and sample size were not supplied.
Result direction: higher concentration is associated with more cash.
No coefficient, uncertainty, mechanism test, or verified citation was supplied.

expectations.description: The missing central magnitude is represented by a conspicuous placeholder.
The descriptive design is expressed with association language.
The response exposes unresolved inputs after the draft.

hard_failures.description: The response must not invent a numeric effect.
The response must not convert the association into a causal finding.
No author-year citation may be invented.

cases.prompt: Audit this conclusion rather than silently rewriting it: 'Our correlations prove the policy improves welfare for every firm.'
provided_facts: The evidence consists of cross-sectional correlations.
No policy variation, causal design, incidence analysis, or welfare benchmark is available.
The requested mode is audit.

expectations.description: Audit output labels the severity or priority of the central problem.
The finding identifies the affected manuscript location.
The audit supplies a concrete strategy rather than diagnosis alone.

hard_failures.description: The response must not endorse the unsupported proof claim.
The response must not retain the unsupported universal welfare claim as valid prose.

cases.prompt: Revise the data and results sections for this return-prediction paper and flag the evidence boundaries.
provided_facts: The signal uses annual accounting data, but the authors sort portfolios in January of the same fiscal year.
The long-short return is 0.7% per month before costs.
No reporting-lag rule, delisting-return treatment, microcap result, shorting cost, or holdout test is supplied.

expectations.description: The response identifies the possible real-time availability failure.
The result is bounded by trading costs, short-leg feasibility, and microcap influence.
The lack of independent validation remains visible.

hard_failures.description: The response must not call the gross return implementable.
The response must not invent a cost-adjusted magnitude.

cases.prompt: Rewrite the interpretation of a new anomaly for RFS without treating a large t-statistic as an explanation.
provided_facts: The high-minus-low return is statistically significant in the discovery sample.
A five-factor model leaves a positive alpha.
No priced-state exposure, belief measure, limits-to-arbitrage interaction, international sample, or post-publication evidence is supplied.

expectations.description: Risk and mispricing remain competing interpretations.
Interpretation strength reflects the missing discriminating evidence.
The response identifies a relevant independent-validation boundary.

hard_failures.description: Benchmark-adjusted alpha alone must not be presented as proof of mispricing.
Statistical strength must not be substituted for an economic mechanism.

cases.prompt: Audit the causal language and redesign the evidence sequence for this staggered-DID results section.
provided_facts: States adopt the policy between 2007 and 2018.
The current regression uses two-way fixed effects with all not-yet and already treated states as controls.
The event-study plot has a visible pre-trend two years before treatment.
No estimator robust to heterogeneous treatment timing or pre-specified remedy is reported.

expectations.description: The audit links staggered timing, heterogeneous effects, and control construction.
The visible pretreatment movement is treated as an identification threat.

values: do not interpret these estimates as identifying
does not support an unqualified causal
expectations.description: Causal wording is downgraded unless the threat is resolved.

hard_failures.description: The response must not claim the stated pre-trend supports parallel trends.

hard_failures.pattern: two-way fixed effects (?:solves|handles|accounts for) heterogeneous treatment effects
hard_failures.description: Conventional TWFE must not be treated as automatically valid under staggered timing.

cases.prompt: Revise the IV interpretation and limitations paragraph for a corporate-finance paper.
provided_facts: The instrument shifts financing access for firms near a lender-specific eligibility rule.
The first-stage F-statistic is supplied as 18.
The exclusion restriction is argued institutionally but cannot be tested directly.
Treatment effects may vary across firms and no monotonicity evidence is supplied.

expectations.description: The supplied first-stage strength is reported without fabrication.

expectations.pattern: exclusion restriction[^.]{0,180}(?:cannot be tested|cannot test|not directly testable|untestable|maintained)
expectations.description: The maintained exclusion restriction is named and bounded.
The estimand is interpreted locally rather than as a universal effect.

hard_failures.pattern: (?:instrument|exclusion restriction) (?:is proven|is definitively exogenous|is unquestionably valid)
hard_failures.description: Institutional reasoning must not be converted into proof of instrument validity.
A potentially local IV estimand must not be generalized to all firms.

cases.prompt: Audit the claim that a funding shock reduces credit supply and propose a defensible results sequence.
provided_facts: Banks with larger deposit outflows originate fewer loans after the shock.
Applications, approvals conditional on application, interest rates, borrower risk, and lender substitution are not reported.
The paper currently calls the loan-volume change a pure credit-supply contraction.

expectations.description: The audit names the missing margins needed to separate supply, demand, and selection.
The proposed evidence sequence pairs price and quantity margins.
The local lender response is bounded by potential substitution.

hard_failures.description: Loan volumes alone must not be relabeled as a pure supply shift.
A lender-level response must not imply an aggregate contraction without substitution evidence.

cases.prompt: Rewrite the interpretation of a market-design result without collapsing liquidity dimensions or making an unsupported welfare claim.
provided_facts: After the venue rule, quoted spreads narrow by 4 basis points.
Market depth falls and realized price impact is unchanged.
No trader-incidence, entry, information-production, or welfare benchmark is supplied.

expectations.description: Each measured liquidity dimension is interpreted separately.
The supplied spread magnitude retains its units.
The absent welfare and incidence evidence is explicit.

hard_failures.description: Mixed liquidity dimensions must not be collapsed into unqualified improvement.
A narrower spread alone must not establish welfare improvement.

cases.prompt: Audit this quantitative-model section for calibration, identification, fit, and counterfactual claim boundaries.
provided_facts: Risk aversion is calibrated from an external paper rather than estimated from the sample.
Three moments are targeted in calibration and the model matches them closely.
No untargeted moments or parameter sensitivity are shown.
A policy counterfactual raises model output by 6%.

expectations.description: The external parameter choice is not mislabeled as sample identification.
Fit to targeted moments is separated from independent validation.
The supplied counterfactual magnitude is labeled model-implied and conditional.

hard_failures.pattern: (?<!not show that )(?<!does not show that )(?<!not establish that )risk aversion is (?:structurally )?identified(?![^.]{0,80}(?:not|rather than))
hard_failures.description: An externally calibrated parameter must not be claimed as identified in-sample.
Target fit alone must not be called independent model validation.
A structural counterfactual must not be recast as a reduced-form causal estimate.

cases.prompt: Revise the proposition intuition and welfare paragraph for a bank-run model; do not invent proof conditions.
provided_facts: The proposition shows a sufficient condition for a unique no-run equilibrium under deposit insurance.
The exact inequality and proof were not supplied.
The policy lowers runs in the model but transfers losses to taxpayers.
Externalities, transition costs, planner information, and distributional weights are not modeled.

expectations.description: The missing formal condition is represented by a visible placeholder.
The supplied logical strength and equilibrium object are preserved.
Welfare interpretation names transfers and omitted social margins.

hard_failures.description: The response must not fabricate the missing mathematical condition.
A reduction in runs must not be treated as sufficient for welfare improvement.
The policy must not be called optimal without a complete welfare benchmark.

cases.prompt: Audit the gross-to-net return sentence without assuming a turnover convention.
provided_facts: The portfolio earns 0.52% per month before costs.
Reported turnover is 190% per month, but the paper does not define whether this is one-side, two-side, or round-trip turnover.
The supplied spread-and-commission estimate is 35 basis points per one-way trade.
The draft reports a numerical net return after silently multiplying by two.

expectations.description: The response makes both the turnover statistic and one-way cost convention visible.
The missing mapping between turnover and trading sides is identified.
A numerical net return is withheld until the convention is supplied.

hard_failures.description: The response must not report the factor-two cost result under an undefined turnover convention.
The response must not invent a numerical net return.

cases.prompt: Audit whether an adverse event-study lead can be explained as anticipation.
provided_facts: Event time minus two is positive and its confidence interval excludes zero.
The policy was announced nine months before implementation.
The calendar dates included in the event-time-minus-two bin are not supplied.
The draft dismisses the lead as announcement anticipation.

expectations.description: The response requires a calendar-time mapping to the announcement.
Anticipation is allowed only if the lead bin overlaps the documented window.
The adverse lead remains an unresolved identifying threat.

hard_failures.description: The response must not call the lead anticipation without a calendar overlap.
The lead must not be endorsed as dismissible under missing timing information.

cases.prompt: Revise the welfare arithmetic for a quantitative model without adding group percentage changes mechanically.
provided_facts: Investor surplus rises 1.3% and dealer surplus falls 1.0% in the counterfactual.
The baseline levels used as denominators for the two percentages are not supplied.
The model separately reports aggregate surplus rising 0.2%.
The draft asks readers to add 1.3% and minus 1.0% to verify the aggregate result.

expectations.description: The response identifies the missing bases for group percentage changes.
The model's aggregation into total surplus must be disclosed.
The aggregate change is retained as a separately reported model output.

hard_failures.description: Group percentage changes with unknown bases must not be added mechanically.
The reported aggregate result cannot be verified from group percentages without denominators.
